QuestionStmt.S: If a statement q has truth value False and $(p \land q) \leftrightarrow r$ has truth value True then which of the following has truth value true?

Solution.S:
Given: $q$ is False.

$(p \land q)$ is False (since $q$ is False).

$(p \land q) \leftrightarrow r$ is True. A biconditional is True only when both sides have the same truth value. Since $(p \land q)$ is False, $r$ must also be False.

Now $p$ can be either True or False.

Check each option:

- Option A: $p \land q$ is False (since $q$ is False).
- Option B: $p \lor r$: $r$ is False, so this equals $p$ (can be True or False, not always True).
- Option C: $p \land r$: $r$ is False, so this is always False.
- Option D: $(p \land r) \to (p \lor r)$: $p \land r$ is False (since $r$ is False). A conditional with a False antecedent is always True, regardless of the consequent. Thus this statement is always True.

Therefore the correct option is D.
